titel: Mouthfeel: how food feels in the mouth
kurz: Besides taste and smell, tongue and palate also feel texture, fat and dryness: this mouthfeel often decides more than the aroma whether we like something.
bild_im_kopf: Like fabric on the skin: the same colour feels quite different as silk than as sackcloth.
was_passiert: The mouth senses whether something is thick or thin, smooth or grainy, crisp or soft. Fat forms a film on the tongue, feels rounded and holds aromas longer. [[gerbstoffe|Tannins]] in red wine, black tea or unripe fruit bind with protein in saliva: the mouth feels dry and furry (astringent).
warum_wichtig: Many kitchen tricks change not the taste but the mouthfeel: butter in a sauce, milk in tea, a spoonful of cream in soup.
faustregeln: If a sauce tastes thin and sharp, it often lacks fat: a knob of cold butter rounds it out.
Milk in black tea softens the furriness because its protein captures the tannins.
For smooth creams and sauces: strain or blend, grains bother us more than a weak flavour.

stellschrauben.wirkung: More fat feels rounder and carries aromas longer

praxis.text: A splash of milk makes strong black tea softer because milk protein binds the tannins.
